import string


def test_decode_shift():
    # Decoding a known encoded string
    assert decode_shift(encode_shift("hello")) == "hello"
    assert decode_shift(encode_shift("world")) == "world"

    # Direct known values: decode_shift shifts each letter back by 5
    assert decode_shift("f") == "a"
    assert decode_shift("a") == "v"
    assert decode_shift("e") == "z"
    assert decode_shift("mjqqt") == "hello"

    # Wrap-around behavior
    assert decode_shift("v") == "q"
    assert decode_shift("z") == "u"

    # Empty string
    assert decode_shift("") == ""

    # Round-trip property over all lowercase letters
    for ch in string.ascii_lowercase:
        assert decode_shift(encode_shift(ch)) == ch

    # Round-trip on a longer mixed string
    original = "thequickbrownfoxjumpsoverthelazydog"
    assert decode_shift(encode_shift(original)) == original

    # Decoding is the inverse of encoding for every letter
    for ch in string.ascii_lowercase:
        encoded = encode_shift(ch)
        assert decode_shift(encoded) == ch
